question: Does the batched GPU geometry implementation reproduce coordinate-invariant differential-geometric quantities on analytic spaces with known answers, within declared numerical tolerances and without cross-candidate contamination?
hypothesis: geometry.candidate.gpu_batched_v1 matches geometry.reference.cpu_v1 and analytic expectations on flat, spherical, and hyperbolic fixtures before any climate interpretation is attempted

datasets.grid: deterministic sample points declared by the runner

units_metadata.policy: dimensionless reference coordinates unless fixture declares a scale

datasets.quality_control_policy: fixture expressions and expected invariants are independently reviewed before promotion

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: all nonsingular sample points across analytic fixtures
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: any unexplained missing result is experiment failure

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: Riemann symmetries, Ricci contraction, and Bianchi witnesses across fixtures
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: missing identity witness is experiment failure

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: matched CPU/GPU diagnostic outputs for identical fixtures and sample points
same candidate executed alone versus in heterogeneous candidate batches
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: missing isolation witness is experiment failure

secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: conditioning must be reported for every inversion path

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: whole fixture suite after correctness gates pass
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: performance is non-authoritative when timing metadata is unavailable

negative_controls: flat polar coordinates must have nonzero Christoffel symbols but zero Riemann/Ricci/scalar curvature
permuting candidate batch order must not alter per-candidate results beyond the declared determinism class
a deliberately ill-conditioned metric fixture added later must produce an explicit conditioning failure or refinement event rather than a plausible-looking curvature result
falsifiers: flat Cartesian or flat polar fixtures produce statistically/numerically meaningful nonzero curvature outside tolerance
sphere or hyperbolic fixtures have the wrong curvature sign or scale after normalization
CPU and GPU implementations disagree outside the conditioning/precision tolerance envelope
a candidate's result changes materially when unrelated candidates are added to the same batch
the implementation silently substitutes a fallback capability while retaining the accelerated implementation identity
split_policy: not applicable; analytic verification suite, with later hidden regression fixtures allowed for implementation hardening
preprocessing: none beyond deterministic coordinate sampling inside declared nonsingular domains
stopping_rule: verification cannot pass until every primary correctness metric satisfies its versioned tolerance on every required fixture; performance comparison is evaluated only after correctness passes
multiple_comparison_policy: not applicable to deterministic analytic verification; any later parameter sweep must report all attempted variants
